overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the May 4 minutes were sufficiently detailed, no executive session occurred, and the remaining allegations were declined as outside the law or not reviewable.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 4 minutes were inaccurate because they did not name the public employee whose conduct he sought to discuss.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the meeting minutes are sufficiently detailed because they adequately summarize the exchange and give a member of the public who did not attend the meeting a clear understanding of what occurred.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council entered executive session on May 4 without a proper statutory purpose to discuss an employee's performance evaluation.
allegations.key_passage: As no executive session took place on May 4, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council President interrupted him and prevented him from speaking during public participation at the May 4 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the City Clerk and Community Media Manager violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The City Clerk and Community Media Manager are individual employees of the City of Medford, not members of public bodies.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged automated closed captioning of the May 4 meeting mis-transcribed his remarks.
allegations.key_passage: As the transcription and closed captioning of meetings is not required by the Open Meeting Law, we also decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Additional allegations raised in the request for further review that were not in the original complaints were not considered.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any additional allegations contained in the request for further review that were not included in the original complaints filed with the public body.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
